messages:
carmen: Heads-up — since the 04:00 driver roll (nv-driver 550) in us-west we've been getting a burst of Xid 45 / Xid 79 and a pile of NCCL watchdog timeouts. Alert fired at 03:11 and noise spiked across 3 clusters. ops-bot posted the deployment: <https://ci.redwood/deploys/550|deploy-550>.

jay: Ugh. Are errors tied to specific instance types or kernels? Any pattern in pod labels?

carmen: Early look shows higher rates on p4d-pool and a few older p3d nodes. Kernel versions seem mixed (5.15 and 6.1) — buckets overlap. Not all pods on the same model.

alex: Can someone grab dmesg + nvidia-smi output from affected nodes and upload? We should also check NCCL logs for watchdog messages. Quick commands:
```
# on node
sudo dmesg | tail -n 300 > /tmp/dmesg-$(hostname).log
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,driver_model,utilization.gpu,clocks.gr --format=csv -f /tmp/gpu-snapshot.csv
kubectl -n gpu logs -l nodepool=p4d --tail=200 | egrep -i "Xid|NCCL|watchdog|NVRM" > /tmp/pod-gpu-errors.log
```

carmen: I'm collecting those now and will upload to gs://redwood-ops/gpu-incident/1891234567/ (will add node list).

ops-bot: deploy-550 completed: 2026-04-02T04:00Z. Canary 10% → 100% in us-west; change: nvidia/driver:550. See <https://ci.redwood/deploys/550|deploy details>.

jay: Thanks. While we collect, we should mute the noisy alert and create a regression alert that tags by driver version — we need to know if 550 is correlated. Current alert is just Xid rate > 5/min for the whole fleet.

alex: Agreed — reduce blast radius: add runbook tag to alert and create temporary alert rule that splits by driver_version. Also add a detector for "NCCL watchdog" substring so we get a separate channel.

sre-oncall: I can flip the alert to a driver-version split and raise threshold to 10/min for 30m to avoid paging while we triage. Oncall will still monitor the driver:550 tag.

carmen: Decision: don't full rollback yet. Plan = 1) collect artifacts from nodes (carmen) 2) run canary rollback to driver:545 in a small subset (alex) 3) add alert split and temp thresholds (sre-oncall) 4) if errors persist in canary, rollback fleet (jay).

alex: I'll prepare a canary job to pin 10 nodes back to driver:545 in us-west-staging by 04:40. Will report results at +20m.

jay: For postmortem instrumentation, we should add permanent telemetry: tag all GPU error events with driver_version and kernel_version, and add a counter for NCCL watchdog per-pod. That'll let us rapidly correlate future rollouts.

carmen: Uploaded artifacts: gs://redwood-ops/gpu-incident/1891234567/dmesg-collection.tar.gz and gpu-snapshots.csv. I also attached a short grep of Xid codes across nodes.

alex: Canary rollback kicked off at 04:41 — targeting p4d-canary. If canary is clean for 20m, we'll schedule a controlled rollback.

sre-oncall: I've updated the alerting rule: "gpu.errors.by_driver" now emits per-driver metrics and added an annotation linking to runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/gpu-driver-regressions. Muted the global Xid pager for 40m.

carmen: Initial canary looks better (no new Xid/NCCL logs in the last 12m). Leaving this thread open for 30m then will file a short incident note.

jay: Great work. After incident, we should add a preflight that runs a small NCCL allreduce smoke test post-driver rollout on a mixed kernel set. If that fails, block rollout.

ops-bot: incident-digest created: <https://incidents.redwood/1891234567|gpu-driver-550-regression>

carmen: Filing follow-up items in T-Infra: add telemetry + preflight + alert-split. Assigning: jay (telemetry), alex (preflight job), carmen (postmortem writeup).

sre-oncall: I'll keep watch for 1h then hand back to infra. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
